title: Palindromic Substrings
keyIdea: Expand around each of the 2n − 1 middles (one letter or two). Every successful step outward is one more palindrome with that middle, so add up how far each middle expands.

approaches.name: DP table
approaches.idea: dp[i][j] = s[i] == s[j] and (length ≤ 2 or dp[i + 1][j − 1]); fill i from n − 1 down and count the true cells.
approaches.why: n(n + 1)/2 cells, each O(1); the table is n × n.

approaches.name: Expand around center
approaches.idea: Your code: expand(center, center) + expand(center, center + 1) for each center; each returns how many palindromes it found.
approaches.why: 2n − 1 middles, each expanding at most n/2 steps; only counters are kept (pass s as const string& to avoid copying).
approaches.warn: The loop checks i < s.length(); it should be j < s.length(). It still works because i only goes down, and when j reaches the end, s[j] is the end character '\0', which never equals a letter.

options: 6: a, a, a, aa, aa, aaa

quiz.q: Why does each successful expansion step add exactly one palindrome?
options: Each step gives a new, longer palindrome with that middle, and no other middle produces it
It doesn't, some are counted twice

quiz.q: In your expand loop, what should the middle condition be?
options: j < s.length() (i only moves left, so i < s.length() is always true)

quiz.q: What is the difference from Longest Palindromic Substring?
options: Same expansion; count every step instead of keeping only the longest
